newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac says housing upswing to continue.
newsitem.headline: Westpac says housing upswing to continue.

text.p: The recovery in Australia's residential property market is set to continue through 1997 but is unlikely to match previous recoveries, Westpac Banking Corp said on Monday.
The bank's latest housing report highlighted a continuing build-up in demand for residential property following a 30 percent fall in interest rates since mid-1996.
Westpac chief economist Nigel Stapledon said the latest mortgage rate cuts in February had pushed housing affordability to new heights, lifting both home buyer and investor confidence.

A Westpac-Melbourne Institute survey showed 69 percent of respondents believed buying conditions were favourable, up from 62 percent in December and just below the record of 71 percent in March 1994, Stapledon said.
The improvement in confidence had been reflected in a strong rise in borrowing but home buyers were unlikely to bid up prices across the board and erode the gains in affordability, he said.
"People's expectations of future wages growth and capital gain on their house are lower now than they were in the mid-1980s," Stapledon said.
Prices would rise in 1997 but would be moderate, mostly confined to the premium end of the market, and more marked in New South Wales and Victoria than other states, the report said.
"While the upcycle in dwelling activity is clearly under way, the view remains that the strength and pace of the upturn wil be less than that of previous recoveries," it said.

However, the recovery would become more pronounced in the second half of 1997. "We expect more synchronised growth to start emerging in late 1997, leading to strong growth (in housing and the broader economy) in 1998," Westpac said.
